title: Turn the booking modal into a real dialog
prompt:
Ticketly's booking modal is a `div` that appears when you press **Book now**. Focus stays behind it, the page underneath stays reachable, and screen readers aren't told a dialog opened.

Convert `#booking` into a native `<dialog>` (keep the id) with an accessible name taken from its heading "Book Friday pass". Open it as a **modal** from the Book now button and close it from the Close button. When it closes, focus should be back on Book now.
hints: Change the div to <dialog> and remove the hidden attribute; a closed dialog is hidden already.
Use modal.showModal() to open and modal.close() to close. The browser moves focus in, makes the page inert, and restores focus on close.
explanation: `showModal()` does the work that used to need a focus-trap library: it moves focus to the first focusable element (the quantity field), makes everything outside the dialog inert so neither Tab nor a screen reader's virtual cursor can wander behind it, closes on Escape, and returns focus to Book now when the dialog closes. `aria-labelledby` makes NVDA announce "Book Friday pass, dialog" on open. Notice that the JavaScript barely changed; the improvement comes from choosing the right element and method.

checks.opens-modal: Book now opens it as a modal dialog
checks.focus-inside: Focus moves inside the dialog when it opens
checks.page-inert: The page behind can't receive focus while the dialog is open
checks.focus-returns: Close closes the dialog and focus returns to Book now
